description: Fixed-point item wider than 18 digits (PIC 9(19)) - the 2002+ wide tier; COBOL-85 caps numeric items and literals at 18 digits. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): 1985 'The number of digit positions that can be described by the PICTURE character-string must range from 1 to 18 inclusive' (§1985:VI.5.9.4 GR3a, numeric; GR6a1 the same for numeric edited) and 'The implementor must allow for numeric literals of 1 through 18 digits in length' (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2); 2002 'For data items of category numeric and numeric-edited, the number of digit positions described by character-string-1 shall range from 1 through 31' (§2002:13.16.38.2 SR6) and 'The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits in length' (§2002:8.3.1.2.2.1), §2002:F.2 item 55 recording 'The maximum number of digits that may be specified in a numeric literal or in a picture character-string that describes a numeric or numeric-edited data item is increased from 18 to 31'. 2014 keeps 31 (§2014:13.18.40.2 SR11; §2014:8.3.1.2.2.1), as does 2023 (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR14; §2023:8.3.3.3.2).
vcr: 85→2002 capacity change (§2002:F.2 item 55: 18 to 31 digits; §2023:8.3.3.3.2 1..31-digit literals)
